title: On-prem Network Drift Intake — Prioritizing Security-Constrained Upgrade Requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a prioritized intake pathway for customer requests that involve network changes or upgrades for on-prem / VPC / air-gapped Redwood Private deployments. Unlike existing intake playbooks that are broad, this aims to handle 'network drift' cases — situations where a customer is requesting incremental network changes (e.g. firewall rule additions, new egress endpoints, proxy certificate rotations, or phased OS/kernel upgrades) that are high-friction due to security policies and limited maintenance windows. The goal is a lightweight but auditable triage rubric that: (1) rapidly classifies risk and rollback complexity, (2) recommends a remediation lane (self-serve, concierge, operator-assisted), and (3) surfaces explicit operator runbooks and compatibility shims required for safe upgrade windows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented triage rubric exists and maps >=90% of recent customer network-change requests to a recommended lane (self-serve / concierge / operator-assisted). 2) Playbook includes a minimum viable set of network probes and a smoke-test matrix customers can run pre-upgrade. 3) Product + BE/Infra + Security sign-off on the scoring thresholds and remediation lane definitions. 4) At least one pilot customer uses the pathway successfully (no critical regressions during upgrade window).
triage_rubric: Score buckets (0-10) computed from: exposure surface (0-4), rollback complexity (0-3), data-sensitivity/regulatory constraints (0-2), and maintenance-window friction (0-1). - 0-2 => Self-serve (docs + automated probe). - 3-6 => Concierge (scheduled runway, SRE assistance, contract ops). - 7-10 => Operator-assisted (onsite/airgap engineer, detailed rollback plan, extended smoke tests). The rubric also flags 'kernel/driver changes' and 'edge-proxy certificate rotations' as automatic escalation points.
technical_notes: Proposed lightweight probes: 1) outbound/ingress endpoint handshake test to the Redwood egress IP set (scripted, deterministic). 2) TLS cert chain verification utility for corporate proxy certs. 3) KV cache validity test to ensure persistent cache behavior across upgrades. Implementation: small Go binary (<=50KB) distributed in a tarball and run in customer environment or via a remote probe agent. Provide an option to run probes from Redwood-managed sandboxed VM for air-gapped customers via shipped offline bundle.

2025-02-18 Marcus Chen: SRE reviewed probes — outbound IP handshake ok but need to limit DNS dependence for airgapped. Suggested adding deterministic IP fallback and TCP handshake only mode.
2025-02-21 Sofia Rivera: Security review requested; must include KMS/HSM impact assessment for upgrades that touch key rotation. Flagging for formal review queue.

2025-02-25 Daniel Park: Suggest adding a 'proxy shim' pattern: small forward-reverse proxy that customers can run for short windows to bridge legacy proxy restrictions; adds rollback complexity but often reduces project time by 40%.
2025-02-28 Marcus Chen: Pilot customer Genomex approved to run probes on 2025-03-05; concierge lane reserved for 2025-03-12 maintenance window.
2025-03-01 Aisha Patel: Updated rubric thresholds after pilot backlog review; increased operator-assisted threshold for kernel/driver changes.
decisions: Adopted the 0-10 scoring rubric for initial rollout (decision logged 2025-02-20).
Default to 'concierge' lane when customer-request involves more than one high-risk change (e.g., cert rotation + firewall change).
Deliver probes as both an online runner and an offline tarball for air-gapped customers to avoid creating new network dependencies.

Formal security review for KMS/rotation impact (owner: Sofia Rivera) - request filed 2025-02-21.
Pilot execution with Genomex and post-mortem capture (owner: Daniel Park) - window 2025-03-05 to 2025-03-12.

risks: Under-scoring complex changes could lead to failed upgrades and increased MTTR.
Probe binaries could be blocked by customer IDS/policy in certain air-gapped environments unless delivered as offline-approved artifacts.
Operator-assisted lane requires staffing plan; without on-call rota changes we could backlog requests.
Legal/regulatory customers may require lengthy legal review before we can ship probes; need red team signoff for any uploaded artifacts.
